FINDING | contract: Raffle | function: _isProtocolDestination | bug_class: time-of-check-destination-bypass | group_key: Raffle | _isProtocolDestination | time-of-check-destination-bypass
invariant: `_isProtocolDestination(addr, prizeToken)` must remain `false` for every accepted `sponsorRecipient`, `protocolTreasury`, and ticket `ownerOf(ticketId)` across the entire raffle lifecycle so that no registered `Raffle` clone owns a ticket or receives an unrecoverable prize and no allocated liability reverts on payout
violation_path: `RaffleFactory.createRaffle` (deploys Raffle 1 at factory nonce 2 with `sponsorRecipient = computeCreateAddress(factory, 3)`, or a buyer calls `Raffle1.buyEntries(computeCreateAddress(factory, 3), 1)`) → `RaffleFactory.createRaffle` (deploys Raffle 2 at factory nonce 3, setting `isRaffle[computeCreateAddress(factory, 3)] = true`) → `Raffle1.releaseSponsorProceeds()` / `Raffle1.releaseSponsorPrize()` / `Raffle1.redeemWinningTicket(1)` / `Raffle1.refundTickets([1])`
path: caller → `RaffleFactory.createRaffle` / `Raffle.buyEntries` with precomputed next-clone address `computeCreateAddress(factory, raffleCount + 2)` → `Raffle._isProtocolDestination` returns `false` because `destination.code.length == 0` and `isRaffle[destination] == false` → next `RaffleFactory.createRaffle` deploys a `Raffle` clone at `destination` and sets `isRaffle[destination] = true` → `_isProtocolDestination(destination, prizeToken)` flips to `true`, causing `releaseSponsorProceeds` to revert with `InvalidQuoteDestination(destination)`, `releaseSponsorPrize` to transfer the prize NFT via `transferFrom` into the new `Raffle` clone where it cannot be rescued, and any ticket minted/transferred to `destination` to permanently lock the NFT prize or USDC liability in `Raffle1`
proof:
1. `RaffleFactory` deploys `raffleImplementation` in its constructor at factory nonce `1`.
2. In `RaffleFactory.createRaffle` for `raffleId = 1`, `Clones.clone(raffleImplementation)` uses `CREATE` at factory nonce `2` (`raffle1 = computeCreateAddress(factory, 2)`).
3. Before `raffleId = 2` is created, `raffle2 = computeCreateAddress(factory, 3)` has `raffle2.code.length == 0` and `factory.isRaffle(raffle2) == false`.
4. Case A (`sponsorRecipient = raffle2`): Sponsor creates `raffle1` with `sponsorRecipient = raffle2` and `reserveEntries = 10`. Both `RaffleFactory._validateCreateParams` (`isRaffle[raffle2] == false`) and `Raffle.initialize` (`_isProtocolDestination(raffle2, prizeToken) == false`) pass. Next, `createRaffle` for `raffleId = 2` deploys `raffle2` at `computeCreateAddress(factory, 3)` and sets `isRaffle[raffle2] = true`. After `raffle1` sells 1 entry (`1_000_000` quote units), resolves to `Status.CashWon`, and settles (`sponsorProceeds = 150_000`), calling `raffle1.releaseSponsorProceeds()` calls `_transferQuote(raffle2, 150_000)`, which now evaluates `_isProtocolDestination(raffle2, address(prizeToken)) == true` and reverts forever with `InvalidQuoteDestination(raffle2)`, leaving `accountedQuoteBalance() >= 150_000` permanently. Calling `raffle1.releaseSponsorPrize()` skips `_isProtocolDestination` and calls `prizeToken.transferFrom(raffle1, raffle2, prizeTokenId)`, locking the NFT inside `raffle2`.
5. Case B (`buyEntries(raffle2, 1)`): While `raffle1` is `Status.Active`, a caller invokes `raffle1.buyEntries(raffle2, 1)` for `1_000_000` quote units. `_update` checks `_isProtocolDestination(raffle2, address(prizeToken))` which is `false`, and `_safeMint` skips `onERC721Received` because `raffle2.code.length == 0`. Once `createRaffle` deploys `raffle2`, `factory.isRaffle(raffle1.ownerOf(1)) == true`. Because `raffle2` has no function to transfer or burn tickets it owns and `_transferQuote(raffle2, ...)` reverts with `InvalidQuoteDestination(raffle2)`, ticket `1` can never be refunded or redeemed; if ticket `1` wins in `Status.NftWon`, `redeemWinningTicket(1)` reverts with `NotTicketOwner` and `releaseSponsorPrize()` reverts with `SponsorPrizeUnavailable(Status.NftWon)`, permanently locking the prize NFT in `raffle1`.
description: A caller can pass the deterministic address of a future raffle clone before deployment, so a later createRaffle call locks the payout or prize.
fix: Deploy clones with Clones.cloneDeterministic and a salt derived from block.prevrandao and msg.sender, and check _isProtocolDestination inside releaseSponsorPrize and redeemWinningTicket.

description: The function clears _requestInFlight before the external refund call, so a callback in that call can resolve the draw early. Standard VRF fulfills across blocks.
